hook.text: Hendrix lost the side one master tape in a London taxi, and most of that side was remixed in one overnight session.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: May to June and October 1967, Olympic Studios, London

sentences.text: Are You Experienced had been finished by late April 1967, and this album came out seven months after that debut's release.
After that, the band kept up its regular recording sessions at Olympic Studios in London.
On May 4 they began composing material for a follow-up LP, starting with a Noel Redding song about hippies called She's So Fine.
Chas Chandler produced and Eddie Kramer engineered, with George Chkiantz as second engineer.
The basic tracks went onto four tracks: drums on two, bass on a third, and rhythm guitar on the fourth.
Chandler, Hendrix and guests Graham Nash and Gary Leeds stomped on a drum riser to create percussion for If 6 Was 9.
Hendrix played recorder on that track too, though he had no formal training on the instrument.
Noel Redding had a tape of the lost mix, and the tape was so wrinkled it had to be pressed flat with an iron.
The Hendrix Estate released a box set, The Jimi Hendrix Experience: Bold As Love Sessions, on 7 November 2025.
It has 66 tracks, among them demos and alternate takes, and both the stereo and the mono mixes of the album.
The Blu-ray in the set includes a Dolby Atmos mix.
Cat Talking to Me, recorded in June 1967, came out later on the posthumous album West Coast Seattle Boy: The Jimi Hendrix Anthology, in 2010.

listen_for.text: Sounds from Hendrix's guitar travel across the stereo image and seem to revolve around you, with feedback running through the track.
Its lyrics came from The Spanish Castle, a dance hall now in Des Moines, Washington, where Hendrix played with local rock bands as a teenager.
Hendrix's guitar runs through a Leslie speaker here, a first for him, and the speaker gives the sound a wavering effect.
Hendrix plays recorder on it, and some of the percussion is Gary Leeds and Graham Nash stomping their feet.
Its guitar works through chordal arpeggios, and the track fades out on tremolo-picked double stops.
